doc.title: James Lincoln Collier interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007

title: Collier's 'Koko' description
summary: Rowe quotes a line Collier wrote about the sixth chorus of Ellington's 'Koko.'

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: We’re going to be running out of tape soon. But this is a great conversation. I wanted to — a couple of things you wrote, one thing I really just want to say is a great little description you wrote of the sixth chorus on Ellington’s recording of “Koko,” you described it as “sounds as if we were opening and closing a door on a cocktail party.”
You said that. That was a good description.
It sounds very nice. I’ll have to bear that in mind.
